'''''Euphorbia terracina''''', commonly known as the '''Geraldton carnation weed''' and '''False [[caper]]''', is a species of perennial herb in the family [[Euphorbiaceae]]. It has a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves. Flowers are visited by ''[[Lipotriches brachysoma]]'', ''[[Lipotriches natalensis]]'', ''[[Lipotriches crassula]]'', and ''[[Nomia bouyssoui]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Euphorbia terracina L. - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/1143778|access-date=2022-02-04|website=eol.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mifsud|first=Stephen|date=2002-08-23|title=Euphorbia terracina (Coastal Spurge) : MaltaWildPlants.com - the online Flora of the Maltese Islands.|url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/EUPH/Euphorbia_terracina.php|access-date=2022-02-16|website=www.maltawildplants.com|language=en-us}}</ref> It produces small, three lobed fruits, with each lobe containing one seed.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Riordan |first1=Erin C. |last2=Rundel |first2=Philip W. |last3=Brigham |first3=Christy |last4=Tiszler |first4=John |date=2008 |title=Morphological Traits and Invasive Potential of the Alien Euphorbia Terracina (euphorbiaceae) in Coastal Southern California |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41425759 |journal=Madroño |volume=55 |issue=1 |pages=52–59 |doi=10.3120/0024-9637(2008)55[52:MTAIPO]2.0.CO;2 |jstor=41425759 |issn=0024-9637}}</ref>
== Distribution ==
''Euphorbia terracina'' is natively distributed in Mediterranean climate regions of Northern Africa, temperate Asia, and some areas of Europe. It is an invasive weed in other similar climate regions mainly in Australia and the U.S. state of California.<ref name=":0">{{Cite report |title=Euphorbia terracina (false caper) |last=CABI |date=2022-01-07 |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.21379 |language=en|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Euphorbia terracina Calflora |url=https://www.calflora.org/app/taxon?crn=8565 |access-date=2024-04-17 |website=www.calflora.org}}</ref> It [[Allelopathy|allelopathically]] inhibits growth of surrounding plants.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Euphorbia terracina Profile – California Invasive Plant Council |url=https://www.cal-ipc.org/plants/profile/euphorbia-terracina-profile/ |access-date=2024-04-17 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Toxicity ==
{{See also|Euphorbia}}
''Euphorbia terracina'' is toxic to both humans and livestock. As with many other Euphorbia species, exposure to its milky sap may cause irritation to skin, eyes, and digestive tracts.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Uses ==
In some regions of Algeria, the sap of ''Euphorbia terracina'' is used to treat warts. The sap has been found to demonstrate [[Antioxidant|antioxidative]] properties<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zeghad |first1=Farida |last2=Djılanı |first2=Salah Eddine |last3=Djılanı |first3=Abdelouaheb |last4=Dıcko |first4=Amadou |date=2016 |title=Antimicrobial and antioxidant activities of three Euphorbia species |url=http://turkjps.org/article_11033/Antimicrobial-And-Antioxidant-Activities-Of-Three-Euphorbia-Species |journal=Turkish Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=22–37 |doi=10.5505/tjps.2016.29491 |issn=1304-530X|doi-access=free }}</ref>
